comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Covenants and Credit Agreement Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: The indentures governing AMD's senior notes and the Assumed Xilinx Notes, along with its $3.0 billion Revolving Credit Agreement, impose covenants that restrict AMD's ability to incur liens, enter into sale-leaseback transactions, merge, or sell substantially all assets. The Revolving Credit Agreement also requires maintenance of a minimum interest coverage ratio and includes cross-default provisions that could accelerate debt repayment if AMD defaults on other material indebtedness, creating liquidity risk if lenders accelerate borrowings.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose that indebtedness covenants restrict corporate actions such as incurring liens, merging, or selling assets. NVDA highlights that covenant breaches can accelerate debt repayment, a risk AMD explicitly addresses through cross-default provisions in its Revolving Credit Agreement and convertible notes. AMD provides more specific detail on the types of restrictions (e.g., sale-leaseback transactions) and the existence of a $3.0 billion facility, whereas NVDA focuses on the general impact of restrictions on business flexibility.

sentences.text: Maintenance of our current and future indebtedness and contractual restrictions could cause us to dedicate a substantial portion of our cash flows from operations towards debt service obligations and principal repayments; increase our vulnerability to adverse changes in general economic, industry and competitive conditions; limit our flexibility regarding changes in our business and our industry; impair our ability to obtain future financing; and restrict our ability to grant liens on property, enter into certain mergers, dispose of our assets, or materially change our business.
If we breach any of the covenants without a waiver from the note holders or lenders, then any outstanding indebtedness may be declared immediately due and payable.

The indenture governing our 3.924% Senior Notes due 2032 and 4.393% Senior Notes due 2052 contains various covenants that limit our ability to, among other things: create liens on certain assets to secure debt, enter into certain sale and leaseback transactions; and consolidate with, merge into or sell, convey or lease all or substantially all of our assets to any other person.

Our Revolving Credit Agreement contains various covenants which limit our ability to, among other things, incur liens; and consolidate or merge or sell our assets as an entirety or substantially as an entirety (in each case, except for certain customary exceptions).

The agreement governing our convertible notes and our Revolving Credit Agreement contains provisions whereby a payment default or acceleration under certain agreements with respect to other material indebtedness would result in cross defaults under our convertible indenture or the Revolving Credit Agreement and allow note holders or the lenders under our Revolving Credit Agreement to declare all amounts outstanding under certain of our indentures or the Revolving Credit Agreement to be immediately due and payable.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of November 3, 2024, the company's aggregate indebtedness was $69,847 million, which exposes it to increased vulnerability to economic conditions, interest rate risk from floating rate loans, competitive disadvantages, and reduced financial flexibility.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and AVGO both identify that maintaining substantial indebtedness requires dedicating significant cash flows to debt service, which reduces liquidity for other business needs and increases vulnerability to adverse economic conditions. AVGO quantifies its exposure with a specific aggregate indebtedness figure ($69,847 million), while NVDA describes the mechanism of risk (dedicating cash flows) without citing a total debt principal in this specific disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Debt Obligations and Capital Return Restrictions
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces risks related to its significant debt obligations ($51.0 billion in senior unsecured notes as of Dec 28, 2024) and cyclical industry nature, which pose risks to its financial condition, including potential credit rating downgrades that have already occurred in 2024. Additionally, Intel has ceased stock repurchases and suspended its quarterly dividend in Q4 2024, with additional restrictions under the CHIPS Act agreement creating uncertainty regarding future dividend payments or share repurchases.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and INTC both warn that changes in credit ratings can negatively impact security value, liquidity, and future financing terms. INTC distinguishes itself by citing specific historical credit rating downgrades suffered in 2024 and their immediate impact on borrowing costs, whereas NVDA states the potential future risk generally without citing past downgrades in this section.

sentences.text: Changes to our credit rating may negatively impact the value and liquidity of our securities, restrict our ability to obtain future financing and affect the terms of any such financing.

These fluctuations, together with our debt level and related debt service obligations, could have the effect of, among other things, reducing our flexibility to respond to changing business and economic conditions and increasing the risk of a future downgrade in our credit ratings that can impact the value of our outstanding debt and increase our borrowing costs.

During 2024 and in prior years, we suffered multiple credit rating downgrades that adversely impacted our borrowing costs and access to capital, and we may continue to suffer additional such downgrades if our business and financial results do not measurably improve.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of August 29, 2024, the company had debt with a carrying value of $13.40 billion and may incur additional debt; these obligations could adversely affect cash flow, credit ratings, borrowing costs, and financial flexibility.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks associated with outstanding and future debt
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm's outstanding debt and any additional debt may negatively impact its business by reducing cash available for other purposes, limiting financing flexibility, and requiring sufficient cash flow from operations to service; inability to generate sufficient cash may force refinancing, asset sales, or reduction of dividends/repurchases, potentially on unfavorable terms or at higher interest rates.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and QCOM both disclose that indebtedness limits financial flexibility and restricts the ability to obtain future financing or react to business changes. Both also note that debt service obligations consume cash that could otherwise be used for other corporate purposes (implied by NVDA's restriction on granting liens/mergers and QCOM's explicit mention of reducing cash available for other purposes).

sentences.text: Maintenance of our current and future indebtedness and contractual restrictions could cause us to dedicate a substantial portion of our cash flows from operations towards debt service obligations and principal repayments; increase our vulnerability to adverse changes in general economic, industry and competitive conditions; limit our flexibility regarding changes in our business and our industry; impair our ability to obtain future financing; and restrict our ability to grant liens on property, enter into certain mergers, dispose of our assets, or materially change our business.
Our ability to comply with the covenants in our indenture may be affected by events beyond our control.

Our outstanding debt and any additional debt we incur may have negative consequences on our business, including, among others: requiring us to use cash to pay the principal of and interest on our debt, thereby reducing the amount of cash available for other purposes; limiting our ability to obtain additional financing for working capital, capital expenditures, acquisitions, stock repurchases, dividends, general corporate or other purposes; and limiting our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business, industries or the market.

Our ability to make payments of principal and interest on our debt depends upon our future performance, which is subject to economic and political conditions, industry cycles and financial, business and other factors, many of which are beyond our control.
